name: Naked Whey Grass-Fed Unflavored (Naked Nutrition)
ingredients_found: 100% Grass-Fed Whey Protein (whey protein concentrate). Single ingredient. No sweeteners, no gums, no lecithin, no added sugar.
reason: Single-ingredient cold-processed grass-fed whey concentrate; zero gums, zero sweeteners, zero added sugar. Engineered/isolated protein caps it at Tier 2 (cannot be Tier 1).
justification: Passes every pre-filter (P1 no emulsifiers/gums, P3 no seed oils, P4 no added sugar), but per P2 a processed whey protein is not a native whole-food matrix, so it is a clean functional tool at Tier 2, not a Gold-Standard whole food.
notes: Unflavored concentrate variant audited. Shipped catalog had this at Tier 1; corrected to Tier 2 because any engineered protein powder cannot be Tier 1.

notes: Audited the Unflavored variant per instructions. Flavored variants add stevia extract (pure) and would still be Tier 2; only the unflavored SKU is scored here.

No unflavored/additive-free version of this brand's isolate was found.
reason: The specific 'Unflavored (RAW Nutrition)' isolate as described (Informed-certified grass-fed isolate) could not be confirmed to exist; the brand's actual isolate is flavored-only and every flavor contains erythritol, a guar/acacia/xanthan gum blend, and steviol glycosides — which would each independently disqualify.
justification: Per the sourcing standard, an ingredient deck that cannot be credibly confirmed is set verified:false / delete_unverifiable; note that if this maps to the real (flavored) RAW Nutrition isolate it fails P1 (gum blend strips the mucin layer) and the sweetener matrix (erythritol polyol + stevia blended with gums).
notes: Brand ambiguity: 'RAW Nutrition' (getrawnutrition.com / CBUM Isolate) is flavored-only with erythritol+gums+stevia (DQ). A different single-ingredient brand 'Raw Organic Whey / Raw Grass Fed Whey' (raworganicwhey.com) IS clean unflavored, but that is a concentrate and is NOT Informed-certified, so it does not match this catalog entry. Unverifiable as specified.

name: Naked Vanilla Grass-Fed Whey (Naked Nutrition)
ingredients_found: Grass-Fed Whey Protein (concentrate), Natural Vanilla Flavor, Organic Coconut Sugar. 5g added sugar per serving.
reason: Added organic coconut sugar (5g/serving) in a protein staple — added sugar in the Clear Whey (savory/staple) category is an L2 disqualifier.
justification: Violates P4 (Glycemic Influx): added sugar in a protein-staple powder floods the hepatic portal vein without a protective whole-food matrix, driving de novo lipogenesis and fluid retention. Clear Whey is a designated staple category, so any added sugar trashes it.
notes: Coconut sugar is still added sugar; 'organic/natural' does not exempt it. Clean of gums/artificial sweeteners, but the added sugar is the disqualifier.

name: Gold Standard 100% Whey - Double Rich Chocolate (Optimum Nutrition)
ingredients_found: Protein Blend (Whey Protein Isolate, Whey Protein Concentrate, Hydrolyzed Whey Protein Isolate), Cocoa (Processed with Alkali), Natural and Artificial Flavor, Lecithin (Sunflower and/or Soy), Salt, Cellulose Gum, Xanthan Gum, Sucralose, Acesulfame Potassium.
reason: Contains sucralose AND acesulfame potassium (synthetic sweeteners) plus cellulose gum AND xanthan gum (gums). Any one of these is a hard disqualifier.
justification: Fails P1 (Mucosal Shielding): cellulose gum and xanthan gum act as detergents on the gut lining, and sucralose/acesulfame-K are synthetic sweeteners flagged as gut-disrupting by the Sweetener Matrix. Trashed regardless of protein quality.
notes: Shipped catalog wrongly kept this at Tier 2 (flags emul+tool) despite sucralose, acesulfame-K, and two gums. Corrected to disqualify.

ingredients_found: Instantized Whey Protein Isolate, Instantized Whey Protein Concentrate, Peanut Flour, Medium Chain Triglyceride Powder (MCTs from Palm Kernel and Coconut Oil, Sodium Caseinate, Silicon Dioxide, Sunflower Lecithin), Organic Agave Inulin, Natural and Artificial Flavor, Salt, Gum Blend (Cellulose Gum, Xanthan Gum, Carrageenan), Sucralose, Acesulfame Potassium.
reason: Sucralose and acesulfame potassium (synthetic sweeteners) + a gum blend (cellulose gum, xanthan gum, carrageenan) + agave inulin (engineered fiber). Multiple independent disqualifiers.
justification: Fails P1 (Mucosal Shielding): carrageenan, cellulose and xanthan gums plus inulin strip the mucin layer and ferment into gas/bloat, and the sucralose/acesulfame-K duo is trashed by the Sweetener Matrix. A compromised ultra-processed tool.
notes: Shipped catalog kept this at Tier 3; per the strict clear-whey rules gums + synthetic sweeteners are hard disqualifiers, so corrected to disqualify.

name: ISO100 Hydrolyzed Whey Isolate - Gourmet Chocolate (Dymatize)
ingredients_found: Hydrolyzed Whey Protein Isolate, Whey Protein Isolate, Cocoa (Processed with Alkali), and less than 2% of: Salt, Soy Lecithin, Natural and Artificial Flavor, Potassium Chloride, Sucralose, Steviol Glycosides (Stevia).
reason: Contains sucralose (synthetic sweetener), and stevia (steviol glycosides) blended with sucralose. Sucralose alone is a hard disqualifier.
justification: Fails the Sweetener Matrix: sucralose is a synthetic sweetener that disrupts the gut microbiome/mucosal barrier (P1), and here it is blended with steviol glycosides — a disqualifying combination independent of protein quality.
notes: Current formulation uses sucralose + steviol glycosides + soy lecithin (the shipped catalog's note about CMC/xanthan appears outdated, but the sucralose still disqualifies it either way).
